title: Registering at Tuskegee and the Oklahoma reputation
summary: At the registrar's office he is warned about his Oklahoma predecessors, including his brother Clarence Fields and Jake Simmons, and meets some careless Oklahoma natives.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So we went on for a little longer and that next fall I did go to Tuskegee, and so after I enrolled I was in the Registrar's office and one of the members--I forget what capacity he was in--but was Wilson, the father of Teddy Wilson, was in this office when I was registering myself, and of course during those days, they had a big oil boom and to sell Oklahomans (inaudible) was there, and when I gave where I was from, the guy says, Captain Neely it was known as, and there were two people from Oklahoma who had a very good reputation who was Jake Simmons and my brother, Clarence Fields. They were older and they were known--around 1920 or something--and everybody remembered them,

and so anyway, they guy said, what are you, are you going to be like the other two. Did you come here just to spend some of your money. I said no, I said I'm asking you now, all I have is my entrance fee and I'm coming here to work my way through school, and he said you Oklahomans don't need anything. I said what are you talking about. So they opened the door and when they opened the door, there was at least three guys back there who were sleeping, and so they had had them in there for something, they'd been into or something, and they didn't care, they were sleeping, and so they woke them up and so I asked them where they were from and thye were from Haskell, Oklahoma, not so far away.
